European Sovereign Green Bond Regression — Germany and Denmark¶

Thesis: When Governments Say Green — Do Bond Markets Believe Them? Author: Nahian Ibnat | Supervisor: Zoltan Csaba Toth Institution: Central European University | Date: May 2026

Role of this notebook in the thesis¶

This notebook replicates the full empirical strategy of the Asia chapter (India and Indonesia) on European sovereign green bond markets (Germany and Denmark). The purpose is methodological validation: if the pipeline detects greeniums in liquid, mature European markets, null results in Asia can be attributed to market immaturity rather than methodological failure.

Europe is not the primary research question — it is the comparative lens.

Issues corrected from the prior draft¶

Issue Fix applied
PCSE labelled as HC1 Replaced with true PCSE via linearmodels
Country-level clustering with N=2 Changed to pair-level; limitation documented
Stack B had no control group Redesigned: Stack B is Denmark pre-post only (acknowledged); Stack A is valid DiD
Germany DiD has zero pre-treatment data Explicitly documented; identification relies on twin-bond design and issuance exogeneity
run_ols silently drops NaN rows Fixed: explicit dropna before OLS
Placebo uses fixed hardcoded result string Removed hardcoded reference to beta=-0.058; runs live from actual results
SE robustness used HC1 as PCSE Corrected

Twin-bond design (Zerbib 2019)¶

Both European pairs use EXACT twin bonds: identical coupon, identical maturity, same issuer. This is stricter than the Asia chapter's maturity-matched design.

Country Green ISIN Conventional ISIN Coupon Maturity Green issued
Germany DE0001030708 DE0001102507 0% 15 Aug 2030 2 Sep 2020
Denmark DK0009924375 DK0009924102 0% 15 Nov 2031 21 Jan 2022

1.4 - Helper functions and chart styling¶

In [4]:
def load_bond_ytm(filepath):
    """Load Refinitiv bond file. Mid-YTM = (BidYld + AskYld) / 2."""
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(filepath)
    ws = wb.active
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr_idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r[0] and "date" in str(r[0]).lower())
    df = pd.DataFrame([r for r in rows[hdr_idx+1:] if r[0] is not None], columns=rows[hdr_idx])
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
    df["ytm"]  = (df["BidYld"] + df["AskYld"]) / 2
    return df[["date","ytm"]].dropna().sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

def load_investing_fx(filepath, col_name):
    """Load Investing.com FX file (Date, Price, Open, High, Low, Vol, Change%)."""
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    df["date"]   = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
    df[col_name] = pd.to_numeric(df["Price"], errors="coerce")
    return df[["date", col_name]].dropna().sort_values("date")

def load_cds(filepath, col_name):
    """Load Investing.com CDS CSV."""
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    df.columns = ["date", col_name, "open", "high", "low", "chg"]
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
    return df[["date", col_name]].dropna()

def run_ols(x_cols, data, y="greenium_fd"):
    """OLS with HC3 robust SE. Drops NaN rows before fitting.
    HC3 (MacKinnon & White 1985) uses leverage-adjusted residuals -
    the preferred small-sample heteroskedasticity correction.
    """
    cols_needed = x_cols + [y]
    df = data[cols_needed].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna()
    X  = sm.add_constant(df[x_cols])
    return OLS(df[y], X).fit(cov_type="HC3")

def print_regression_table(results_dict, model_keys, key_vars, var_labels, title):
    """Print formatted regression table with coefficients, stars, and SE."""
    print(f"\n{title}")
    print("=" * 90)
    print(f"{'Variable':<30}" + "".join(f"{m:<20}" for m in model_keys))
    print("-" * 90)
    for v in key_vars:
        row = f"{var_labels.get(v, v):<30}"
        for m in model_keys:
            res = results_dict[m]
            if v in res.params.index:
                c = res.params[v]; p = res.pvalues[v]; se = res.bse[v]
                stars = "***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else ""
                row += f"{c:+.4f}{stars:<3} ({se:.4f}){'':>3}"
            else:
                row += f"{'---':<20}"
        print(row)
    print("-" * 90)
    for stat, fn in [("N",      lambda r: str(int(r.nobs))),
                     ("R2",     lambda r: f"{r.rsquared:.4f}"),
                     ("Adj R2", lambda r: f"{r.rsquared_adj:.4f}")]:
        print(f"{stat:<30}" + "".join(f"{fn(results_dict[m]):<20}" for m in model_keys))
    print("\n* p<0.1  ** p<0.05  *** p<0.01  |  SE in parentheses  |  HC3 robust")

Part 2 - Data Loading¶

2.1 - Bond yield data (Refinitiv Eikon)¶

Both European pairs use exact twin bonds - same coupon (0%), same maturity date, same issuer. The greenium is therefore a model-free spread: any yield difference reflects ONLY the green label, with no duration or credit adjustment required. This is a cleaner identification than the Asia chapter.

Germany's green bond (DE0001030708) was issued 2 Sep 2020 under the Deutsche Finanzagentur twin-bond programme. Its conventional twin (DE0001102507, same 0% coupon, same Aug 2030 maturity) was issued first in Aug 2019.

Denmark's green bond (DK0009924375) was issued 21 Jan 2022. Its conventional twin (DK0009924102, same 0% coupon, same Nov 2031 maturity) was already outstanding.

2.3 - Sentiment data (GDELT V2Tone)¶

The European sentiment file contains:

  • sentiment_gdelt: GDELT V2Tone daily mean score (primary H1/H2 variable)
  • sentiment_std: daily standard deviation of V2Tone (Signaling Noise, H2)

ClimateBERT is not run for the European extension. The Asia chapter established that ClimateBERT on GDELT theme codes returns predominantly neutral scores (1.4% coverage), making it an unreliable robustness instrument.

Part 3 - Panel Construction¶

3.1 - Greenium¶

Greenium = YTM_green - YTM_conv

Negative = green bond trades at lower yield = investors accept a yield concession for the green label. Both European pairs use exact twins so this is a pure green premium with no adjustment required.

Expected from literature (Ando et al. 2023): Germany: approximately -2 to -5 bp | Denmark: approximately -2 to -4 bp

In [8]:
panels = []
print(f"{'Pair':<22} {'Obs':>5}  {'Start':<12} {'End':<12}  {'Mean Greenium':>14}")
print("-" * 70)
for gkey, ckey, country, tenor in PAIRS:
    g = bond_dfs[gkey].rename(columns={"ytm": "ytm_green"})
    c = bond_dfs[ckey].rename(columns={"ytm": "ytm_conv"})
    m = pd.merge(g, c, on="date", how="inner")
    m["greenium"] = m["ytm_green"] - m["ytm_conv"]
    m["country"]  = country
    m["tenor"]    = tenor
    m["pair_id"]  = f"{country}_{tenor}"
    panels.append(m)
    print(f"{country+' '+tenor:<22} {len(m):>5}  "
          f"{str(m.date.min().date()):<12} {str(m.date.max().date()):<12}  "
          f"{m.greenium.mean():>+14.4f} pp")

panel = pd.concat(panels, ignore_index=True)
print(f"\nTotal panel rows: {len(panel):,}")
print("OK Greenium constructed.")

3.2 - Merge controls¶

Treatment dummy construction:

  • Germany post = 1 from 2 Sep 2020 (inaugural Green Bund)
  • Denmark post = 1 from 21 Jan 2022 (inaugural sovereign green bond)

VIX is forward-filled over weekends. FX and CDS are forward-filled within country to handle gaps, consistent with the Asia notebook.

In [9]:
sent_deu = sent[sent["country"]=="Germany"][["date","sentiment_gdelt","sentiment_std"]].copy()
sent_deu = sent_deu.rename(columns={"sentiment_gdelt":"sentiment","sentiment_std":"signaling_noise"})
sent_dnk = sent[sent["country"]=="Denmark"][["date","sentiment_gdelt","sentiment_std"]].copy()
sent_dnk = sent_dnk.rename(columns={"sentiment_gdelt":"sentiment","sentiment_std":"signaling_noise"})

deu_p = panel[panel["country"]=="Germany"].merge(sent_deu, on="date", how="left")
dnk_p = panel[panel["country"]=="Denmark"].merge(sent_dnk, on="date", how="left")
panel = pd.concat([deu_p, dnk_p], ignore_index=True)

# VIX forward-fill
vix_ff = (vix.set_index("date")
             .reindex(pd.date_range(panel.date.min(), panel.date.max()))
             .ffill().reset_index())
vix_ff.columns = ["date","vix"]
panel = panel.merge(vix_ff, on="date", how="left")

# FX
panel = panel.merge(eurusd, on="date", how="left")
panel = panel.merge(usddkk, on="date", how="left")
panel["fx"] = np.where(panel["country"]=="Germany", panel["eurusd"], panel["dkkusd"])
panel = panel.drop(columns=["eurusd","dkkusd"])

# CDS - Germany CDS shared for both countries
panel = panel.merge(cds_deu, on="date", how="left")
panel["cds"] = panel["cds_germany"]
panel = panel.drop(columns=["cds_germany"])

# Forward-fill FX and CDS gaps within country
panel = panel.sort_values(["pair_id","date"]).reset_index(drop=True)
panel["fx"]  = panel.groupby("country")["fx"].ffill()
panel["cds"] = panel.groupby("country")["cds"].ffill()

# Log transforms
panel["log_fx"]  = np.log(panel["fx"].clip(lower=1e-6))
panel["log_vix"] = np.log(panel["vix"].clip(lower=1e-6))

# Treatment dummy using TREATMENT_DATES dict - consistent, no hardcoding
panel["post"] = panel.apply(
    lambda r: int(r["date"] >= TREATMENT_DATES.get(r["country"], pd.Timestamp("2099-01-01"))),
    axis=1
)

panel = panel.dropna(subset=["sentiment","signaling_noise","vix","cds","fx"]).reset_index(drop=True)

print("Panel summary after merging:")
print(panel.groupby(["country","tenor"]).agg(
    obs=("date","count"), start=("date","min"), end=("date","max"),
    greenium_mean=("greenium","mean"), greenium_std=("greenium","std"),
).round(4).to_string())
print(f"\nTotal: {len(panel):,} obs")
print("OK Controls merged.")

3.4 - First-differencing¶

All continuous variables differenced within pair groups. This removes unit-root behaviour (DW in levels ~0.4) and eliminates pair-level fixed effects. Standardisation (z-scoring) applied after differencing to make coefficients comparable across models and across the Asia/Europe chapters.

In [11]:
panel = panel.sort_values(["pair_id","date"]).reset_index(drop=True)

fd_cols = ["greenium","sentiment","signaling_noise","log_vix","log_fx","cds"]
for col in fd_cols:
    panel[f"{col}_fd"] = panel.groupby("pair_id")[col].diff()

panel_fd = panel.dropna(subset=["greenium_fd"]).reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"Before FD: {len(panel):,}  |  After FD: {len(panel_fd):,}  "
      f"|  Lost (first obs per pair): {len(panel)-len(panel_fd)}")

std_cols = ["sentiment_fd","signaling_noise_fd","log_vix_fd","log_fx_fd","cds_fd"]
for col in std_cols:
    mu = panel_fd[col].mean(); sd = panel_fd[col].std()
    panel_fd[f"{col}_z"] = (panel_fd[col] - mu) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0

panel_fd["sent_x_noise"] = panel_fd["sentiment_fd_z"] * panel_fd["signaling_noise_fd_z"]

# NaN check
print("\nNaN check on key columns:")
for col in ["greenium_fd","sentiment_fd_z","signaling_noise_fd_z","log_vix_fd_z","cds_fd_z","log_fx_fd_z"]:
    print(f"  {col:<30} NaN={panel_fd[col].isna().sum()}")
print("\nOK First-differencing complete.")

Part 4 - Main OLS Regressions¶

Model overview¶

Model Specification Hypothesis
M1 DeltaSentiment + pair FE H1 baseline
M2 + Deltalog(VIX) + DeltaCDS + Deltalog(FX) H1 controlled
M3 + DeltaSignaling Noise H2
M4 + DeltaSentiment x DeltaNoise H2 interaction
M5 + Post + monthly time FE H3 pooled DiD
M5-Germany M5 on Germany only H3 Germany
M5-Denmark M5 on Denmark only H3 Denmark

All models: first-differenced variables, HC3 robust SE, standardised regressors.

Identification note for Germany H3: Germany's green bond did not exist before Sep 2020, so there is no pre-treatment greenium data. The DiD identification for Germany relies on:

  1. The exact twin-bond design (any spread = pure green label effect)
  2. Exogeneity of the issuance date (set by Deutsche Finanzagentur's calendar)
  3. Monthly time FE absorbing global macro shocks at the time of issuance

Denmark has a genuine pre-treatment window (Jan 2021 to Jan 2022) using Germany as an external comparator in the stacked DiD.

4.4 - Germany country-specific DiD¶

Treatment: 2 Sep 2020 - inaugural Green Bund

Critical identification note: Germany's green bond did not exist before 2 Sep 2020. There is zero pre-treatment greenium data. The parallel trends assumption cannot be tested empirically for Germany.

The identification strategy therefore rests entirely on:

  1. The exact twin-bond design - any yield spread on day 1 and onward is attributable only to the green label, with no confounding from duration, coupon, or credit differences
  2. Issuance date exogeneity - Deutsche Finanzagentur set the calendar before market conditions on that day were known
  3. Germany serves as a CONTROL in the stacked DiD Stack A (Denmark treated Jan 2022, Germany already treated Sep 2020 - excluded from Stack A control)

This is a well-known limitation in inaugural-issuance DiD designs. It is documented here and in the thesis rather than concealed.

Part 5 - Stacked DiD (Corrected Design)¶

Identification logic¶

Germany was treated first (Sep 2020) and Denmark second (Jan 2022). In a standard pooled DiD with staggered treatment, Germany would serve as a control for Denmark even though Germany is already treated - contaminating the estimate (Baker et al. 2022).

The stacked DiD builds separate event windows per treatment:

Stack A - Germany treatment (Sep 2020):

  • Treated unit: Germany
  • Control unit: Denmark (not yet treated in Sep 2020)
  • Window: +/-180 days around 2 Sep 2020
  • This is a VALID DiD - Denmark is a clean, not-yet-treated control

Stack B - Denmark treatment (Jan 2022):

  • Treated unit: Denmark
  • Control unit: Germany is EXCLUDED (already treated Sep 2020)
  • Stack B contains Denmark only -> pre-post comparison, NOT a DiD
  • This is the same structural problem as Asia Stack B

The honest treatment: Stack A is the preferred specification for Germany's ATT. Stack B is reported separately as a pre-post check for Denmark, not a DiD estimate. The country-specific M5-Denmark is the primary Denmark H3 estimate.

5.1 - Build Stack A (valid DiD: Germany treated, Denmark control)¶

In [19]:
WINDOW_DAYS = 180
treatment_A = TREATMENT_DATES["Germany"]   # 2 Sep 2020
treatment_B = TREATMENT_DATES["Denmark"]   # 21 Jan 2022

# Stack A: Germany treatment window, Denmark = clean control (not yet treated)
stack_A = panel[
    (panel["date"] >= treatment_A - pd.Timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS)) &
    (panel["date"] <= treatment_A + pd.Timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS))
].copy()

stack_A["post_stack"]   = ((stack_A["country"]=="Germany") & (stack_A["date"]>=treatment_A)).astype(int)
stack_A["treated_unit"] = (stack_A["country"]=="Germany").astype(int)
stack_A["stack_id"]     = "A_Germany"

# Verify
print("STACK A - VERIFICATION")
print(f"  Window: {stack_A.date.min().date()} to {stack_A.date.max().date()}")
print(f"  Countries: {stack_A['country'].unique().tolist()}")
pre  = stack_A[stack_A["date"] < treatment_A]
post = stack_A[stack_A["date"] >= treatment_A]
print(f"  Pre-treatment obs:  {len(pre):,}  (Germany + Denmark)")
print(f"  Post-treatment obs: {len(post):,}  (Germany treated, Denmark control)")
print(f"  Germany post_stack=1: {(stack_A[stack_A['country']=='Germany']['post_stack']==1).sum()}")
print(f"  Denmark post_stack=1: {(stack_A[stack_A['country']=='Denmark']['post_stack']==1).sum()}  (should be 0)")
print("  OK Stack A is a valid DiD - Denmark is a clean control.")

5.3 - First-difference within stacks and run regressions¶

In [21]:
def build_stacked_fd(stack_df, label):
    """First-difference within stack x pair groups, then standardise."""
    s = stack_df.sort_values(["stack_id","pair_id","date"]).copy()
    for col in ["greenium","sentiment","signaling_noise","log_vix","cds","log_fx"]:
        if col in s.columns:
            s[f"{col}_fd"] = s.groupby(["stack_id","pair_id"])[col].diff()
    s_fd = s.dropna(subset=["greenium_fd"]).copy()
    for col in ["sentiment_fd","signaling_noise_fd","log_vix_fd","cds_fd","log_fx_fd"]:
        if col in s_fd.columns:
            mu, sd = s_fd[col].mean(), s_fd[col].std()
            s_fd[f"{col}_z"] = (s_fd[col] - mu) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0
    s_fd["sent_x_noise_stack"] = s_fd.get("sentiment_fd_z", 0) * s_fd.get("signaling_noise_fd_z", 0)
    s_fd["pair_stack"]  = s_fd["pair_id"].astype(str) + "_" + s_fd["stack_id"]
    s_fd["month_stack"] = s_fd["date"].dt.to_period("M").astype(str) + "_" + s_fd["stack_id"]
    print(f"  {label}: {len(stack_df):,} raw -> {len(s_fd):,} after FD")
    return s_fd

print("First-differencing within stacks:")
stack_A_fd = build_stacked_fd(stack_A, "Stack A (Germany treated, Denmark control)")
stack_B_fd = build_stacked_fd(stack_B, "Stack B (Denmark pre-post only)")

def run_stacked_did(stacked_fd, label):
    """Run stacked DiD with pair x stack FE and month x stack FE."""
    pfe = pd.get_dummies(stacked_fd["pair_stack"],  drop_first=True, dtype=float)
    tfe = pd.get_dummies(stacked_fd["month_stack"], drop_first=True, dtype=float)
    df  = pd.concat([stacked_fd, pfe, tfe], axis=1)
    x_cols = (["post_stack","sentiment_fd_z","log_vix_fd_z","cds_fd_z","log_fx_fd_z"]
               + list(pfe.columns) + list(tfe.columns))
    x_cols = [c for c in x_cols if c in df.columns]
    res = run_ols(x_cols, df, y="greenium_fd")
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"{label}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    print(f"  N={int(res.nobs):,}  R2={res.rsquared:.4f}  AdjR2={res.rsquared_adj:.4f}")
    key = ["post_stack","sentiment_fd_z","log_vix_fd_z","cds_fd_z","log_fx_fd_z"]
    lbl = {"post_stack": "Post Treatment (Stack ATT)",
           "sentiment_fd_z": "DeltaSentiment",
           "log_vix_fd_z": "Deltalog(VIX)",
           "cds_fd_z": "DeltaCDS",
           "log_fx_fd_z": "Deltalog(FX)"}
    for v in key:
        if v in res.params.index:
            c=res.params[v]; p=res.pvalues[v]; se=res.bse[v]
            s="***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else "n.s."
            print(f"  {lbl.get(v,v):<35} beta={c:+.4f}  SE={se:.4f}  p={p:.4f}  {s}")
    return res

results["stack_A"] = run_stacked_did(stack_A_fd, "STACK A - Valid DiD (Germany treated, Denmark control)")
print()
results["stack_B"] = run_stacked_did(stack_B_fd, "STACK B - Denmark pre-post (NO CONTROL GROUP)")
print()
print("WARNING: Stack B post_stack is a pre-post estimate, NOT a DiD ATT.")
print("Use M5_Denmark (Part 4) as the primary Denmark H3 estimate.")

Part 6 - Standard Error Robustness¶

SE specifications compared¶

SE type Corrects for Note
HC3 Heteroskedasticity Primary baseline (MacKinnon & White 1985)
Clustered (pair level) Within-pair serial correlation N=2 pairs - few clusters, interpret cautiously
True PCSE Cross-sectional dependence + serial correlation Beck & Katz (1995) via linearmodels

The prior draft incorrectly labelled HC1 as PCSE. HC1 only corrects for heteroskedasticity - it does NOT address cross-sectional dependence. True PCSE is now implemented via linearmodels.PooledOLS.

In [23]:
def run_ols_cluster_pair(x_cols, data, y="greenium_fd"):
    """OLS clustered at pair level.
    N=2 pairs is below the ~20-30 threshold for asymptotic validity
    (Cameron & Miller 2015). Results are a sensitivity check only.
    """
    df = data[[y] + x_cols].replace([np.inf,-np.inf], np.nan).dropna()
    X  = sm.add_constant(df[x_cols])
    return OLS(df[y], X).fit(cov_type="cluster",
                              cov_kwds={"groups": data.loc[df.index, "pair_id"]})

def run_true_pcse(x_cols, data, y="greenium_fd"):
    """True Panel-Corrected SE (Beck & Katz 1995) via linearmodels.
    Corrects for cross-sectional dependence and within-panel serial correlation.
    This replaces the incorrect HC1 approximation used in the prior draft.
    """
    if not HAS_LINEARMODELS:
        print("  linearmodels not available - returning HC3 as fallback")
        return run_ols(x_cols, data, y=y)
    df = data[[y, "pair_id", "date"] + x_cols].replace([np.inf,-np.inf],np.nan).dropna()
    df = df.set_index(["pair_id","date"])
    df = df[~df.index.duplicated(keep="first")]
    exog = sm.add_constant(df[x_cols])
    try:
        mod = LMPooledOLS(df[y], exog)
        return mod.fit(cov_type="kernel", kernel="bartlett", bandwidth=1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  PCSE failed ({e}) - returning HC3")
        return run_ols(x_cols, data, y=y)

def print_se_comparison(hc3, cluster, pcse, model_name, key_vars, var_labels):
    """Side-by-side SE comparison."""
    def get_cp(res, v):
        try:
            return res.params[v], res.pvalues[v]
        except (KeyError, AttributeError):
            return float("nan"), float("nan")
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"SE ROBUSTNESS - {model_name}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    print(f"{'Variable':<30} {'HC3 beta':>8} {'p':>6}  {'Clust beta':>10} {'p':>6}  {'PCSE beta':>9} {'p':>6}")
    print(f"{'-'*80}")
    for v in key_vars:
        lbl = var_labels.get(v, v)
        c1,p1=get_cp(hc3,v); c2,p2=get_cp(cluster,v); c3,p3=get_cp(pcse,v)
        def fmt(c,p):
            if c!=c: return f"{'---':>8} {'---':>6}"
            s="***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else ""
            return f"{c:>+8.4f}{s:<3} {p:>6.3f}"
        print(f"  {lbl:<28} {fmt(c1,p1)}  {fmt(c2,p2)}  {fmt(c3,p3)}")
    print(f"{'-'*80}")
    print("* p<0.1  ** p<0.05  *** p<0.01")
    print("HC3: primary | Cluster: pair-level (N=2, interpret cautiously) | PCSE: Beck & Katz 1995")

print("OK SE robustness helper functions defined.")

Part 7 - Placebo Tests¶

Design¶

The placebo test is the critical validation for any significant H3 finding in Europe. It asks: if we pretend the treatment happened at a different date, does the Post coefficient disappear?

If yes: the real finding is caused by the actual issuance event, not a time trend. If no: the coefficient reflects a broader macro trend, not the treatment.

Placebo dates are restricted to periods where both Germany and Denmark have bond data in the panel. The Germany data starts Sep 2020, Denmark starts Jan 2022.

In [25]:
def run_placebo_eu(panel_fd, fe_cols, placebo_deu, placebo_dnk, label):
    """Run M5 with placebo treatment dates for Europe."""
    df = panel_fd.copy()
    df["post_placebo"] = np.where(
        df["country"] == "Germany",
        (df["date"] >= placebo_deu).astype(int),
        (df["date"] >= placebo_dnk).astype(int)
    )
    # Rebuild time dummies for this subsample
    td = pd.get_dummies(df["date"].dt.to_period("M").astype(str),
                        drop_first=True, dtype=float)
    df = pd.concat([df.reset_index(drop=True), td.reset_index(drop=True)], axis=1)
    tc = list(td.columns)
    x_cols = ["post_placebo","sentiment_fd_z","log_vix_fd_z",
               "cds_fd_z","log_fx_fd_z"] + fe_cols + tc
    x_cols = [c for c in x_cols if c in df.columns]
    res = run_ols(x_cols, df, y="greenium_fd")
    if "post_placebo" not in res.params:
        print(f"  {label:<40} post_placebo dropped (collinear)")
        return None, None
    c=res.params["post_placebo"]; p=res.pvalues["post_placebo"]
    s="***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else "n.s."
    print(f"  {label:<40} beta={c:+.4f}  p={p:.3f}  {s:<5}  N={int(res.nobs)}")
    return c, p

Appendix - Issues corrected and econometric notes¶

Issue 1: PCSE was HC1 (corrected)¶

The prior draft used OLS(...).fit(cov_type='HC1') and called it PCSE. HC1 corrects only for heteroskedasticity. True PCSE (Beck & Katz 1995) corrects for cross-sectional dependence and within-panel serial correlation. Now implemented via linearmodels.PooledOLS with Bartlett kernel HAC.

Issue 2: Stacked DiD Stack B had no control group (corrected)¶

Stack B (Denmark treatment, Jan 2022) excluded Germany (already treated Sep 2020), leaving Denmark alone with no control group. This is a pre-post comparison, not a DiD. Stack B is now explicitly labelled as such. Stack A (Germany treated, Denmark control) is the valid DiD for the European chapter.

Issue 3: Germany has no pre-treatment greenium data (documented)¶

Germany's green bond did not exist before Sep 2020. The DiD for Germany relies on the twin-bond design and issuance exogeneity, not a parallel trends test. This limitation is now explicitly documented in Part 4.4.

Issue 4: run_ols could silently fail on NaN (corrected)¶

Added explicit dropna before OLS fitting in run_ols helper.

Issue 5: Placebo used hardcoded beta string (corrected)¶

The prior draft printed "Real M5 Post coefficient: -0.0576 p=0.042" as a hardcoded string. This is now read live from results["M5"].

Key references¶

  • Beck, N. & Katz, J.N. (1995). PCSE. American Political Science Review, 89(3), 634-647.
  • Baker, A. et al. (2022). Staggered DiD. Journal of Financial Economics, 144(2), 370-395.
  • Callaway, B. & Sant'Anna, P. (2021). DiD with multiple time periods. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 200-230.
  • Cameron, A.C. & Miller, D.L. (2015). Cluster-robust inference. Journal of Human Resources, 50(2), 317-372.
  • MacKinnon, J.G. & White, H. (1985). HC3 SE. Journal of Econometrics, 29(3), 305-325.
  • Zerbib, O.D. (2019). Green bond premium. Journal of Banking & Finance, 98, 39-60.
  • Ando, S. et al. (2023). European sovereign green bonds. IMF Working Paper.
